:::{#rem-gradient-flow-euler}
#### Gradient descent is Euler's method for the gradient flow

[Gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent) with a fixed [step length](#def-gradient-descent) $\steplen$ updates
$\iterpoint{\vx}{t+1} = \iterpoint{\vx}{t} - \steplen\,\deriv{\vx} f(\iterpoint{\vx}{t})$.
This is Euler's method with time step $\steplen$ for the [gradient flow](#def-gradient-flow) equation.

For a [linear function](algebra.qmd#def-linear-function) $f$,
the velocity of the flow is the negative [normal vector](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-normal-vector).

By [this theorem](vector-calculus.qmd#thm-level-sets-linear),
that vector is [orthogonal](linear-algebra-vectors.qmd#def-orthogonal-vectors) to every [level set](vector-calculus.qmd#def-level-set),
so the flow is too.

:::
